title: In vitro degradation and biocompatibility evaluation of typical biodegradable metals (Mg/Zn/Fe) for the application of tracheobronchial stenosis

nodes.label: A paediatric tracheobronchial stent must hold the airway for 3-12 months and then vanish; permanent stents provoke granulation
Degradation of the candidate biodegradable metals has never been assessed in an airway fluid or against airway epithelium
Gamble's solution, lower in chloride and richer in bicarbonate and mucin than SBF, should degrade these metals more moderately and rank them for airway use
High-purity Mg, high-purity Zn and pure Fe as the three candidate degradable stent metals

attrs.reason: the three established biodegradable metal families

nodes.label: Two media (GS vs SBF) x three metals x immersion at 7/14/21/28 d; three culture modes DC/IC/EC
Use Gamble's solution as the respiratory-tract simulant and A549 airway epithelial cells as the biological test system

attrs.note: the headline methodological move of the paper

nodes.label: Disks 10 mm x 2 mm cut and ground to 2000 grit SiC
Static immersion in GS or SBF at 37 C, 20 mL/cm2, up to 28 d
Corrosion layers are carbonate plus phosphate; the GS layers on Mg and Zn carry far less P and Ca than the SBF layers
HP-Mg attack spreads over the whole surface within 14 d, while HP-Zn and P-Fe stay largely localised
28-d corrosion rate in GS is well below SBF: 0.78 vs 2.01 (Mg), 0.03 vs 0.10 (Zn), 0.09 vs 0.13 mm/y (Fe)
HP-Mg is ~240 mV nobler and carries ~12x lower corrosion current in GS than in SBF; Zn and Fe differ little between media
A549 viability with HP-Mg and HP-Zn reaches the negative control by day 5, while P-Fe under indirect and extraction culture collapses
GS mucin suppresses phosphate deposition but its low chloride and bicarbonate buffering limit pitting and hold the pH near neutral, so Mg corrodes slower than in SBF
Cytotoxicity tracks the released ion dose: 1.52 mM Fe in the extract is toxic to A549 while 6.03 mM Mg and 0.23 mM Zn are not
HP-Mg and HP-Zn degrade slowly enough and remain benign enough for a temporary airway stent; P-Fe is disqualified by its A549 toxicity
In an airway-simulating fluid HP-Zn and HP-Mg are the viable degradable tracheobronchial stent metals, and SBF overstates their degradation
Ecorr: HP-Mg -1.52 V in GS against -1.76 V in SBF; HP-Zn -1.20/-1.26; P-Fe -0.69/-0.78 V vs SCE

nodes.label: Static immersion without airflow or mucociliary clearance and an A549 monolayer bound how far these rates transfer to an implanted airway stent
The A549 response to P-Fe disagrees with an earlier report that Fe stents stimulate L929 and ECV304 proliferation
Porcine stomach mucin co-precipitates with phosphate and strongly suppresses phosphate deposition
SBF holds about 1.3x the chloride of GS and far less bicarbonate (Table 2)
Fe-based stents were reported to stimulate proliferation of L929 and ECV304 cells
A paediatric airway stent has to support the lumen for 3-12 months

notes: Screening paper: one immersion branch (b9/b10 -> b11/b12) and one cell branch (b13), meeting at the stent-suitability claim b17. b6 (Gamble's solution + A549) is spine as the headline methodological move and realizes the immersion that makes the rate measurable. Audits: a1 (the 14-d HP-Zn-SBF panel shows continuous, not discrete, attack), a2 (text-silent: the GS/SBF rate gap collapses from 26x at 7 d to 2.6x at 28 d, so 'GS is milder' is a short-term statement). c10 records that GS is not the more alkaline medium at late times, which the pathway claim has to accommodate. Packet F4's caption is corrupted: it concatenates a fragment of the Fig. 1 discussion with the Fig. 4 caption. Packet F5 (cell SEM/fluorescence) is tier C with no panels offered and was not opened, so cell morphology is carried only through the CCK-8 node. Lost: Tables 1-2 medium compositions, the LSCM/SEM cell morphology panels, and the 21-d intermediate points.

changes: c7 and a2: provenance derived -> measured. Both read the F3c weight-loss corrosion rate, whose input weight losses are not OBS nodes in this graph, and v04 requires an incoming derives edge for derived. image_note on each now says so.

a1: label overstated the audit as 'broad continuous dark patches'. F2b panel D shows a branching, connected network of dark streaks over most of the field - distributed, not solid coverage. Label and image_note rewritten so the audit says what the panel shows; the point against b10 ('HP-Zn stays largely localised') stands.

panel_checks.note: Day-5 bars measured: HP-Mg-DC 2.32, HP-Zn-DC 2.2, HP-Mg-EC 2.5, negative control 2.58, P-Fe-IC 0.45, P-Fe-EC 0.9 - the node's numbers exactly. Its image_note is also right: HP-Mg-IC reaches 3.32, well above the negative control, which the text passes over.

F4a (HP-Mg): GS starts at 8.4 on day 1 and settles to 7.0-7.1 by day 27, SBF starts 7.75 and holds 7.3-7.5. The ordinate runs to 10.0 but no trace goes above 8.5, so the node's 'no trace rises above 8.5' and 'GS ends below SBF' are both right - which matters, because the pathway claim b15 cannot lean on GS being the more alkaline medium at late times.

Panel ids right - HP-Zn-SBF is panel D of the 2x3 grid in both F2a (7 d) and F2b (14 d), so citing both is the correct way to carry a before/after audit. The reading needed tempering (see changes) but the audit holds.

Extra check. F2a row order is HP-Mg / HP-Zn / P-Fe with GS left and SBF right. HP-Mg-GS (A) shows discrete dark pits on a still-ground surface, HP-Mg-SBF (B) a continuous cracked layer, and the only 10 um inset is on the HP-Mg-GS panel, exactly as the image_note says.

review.audit_summary: 2 audits plus a DSC/limitation and a DSC/comparison - well inside budget and each earns its place. a1 is a fair 'figure contradicts text' on the localisation claim, now worded to match the panel. a2 is the strongest audit in the paper and is correctly marked text_silent: the GS/SBF corrosion-rate gap collapses from ~26x at 7 d to ~2.6x at 28 d, so the headline 'GS is milder' is a short-term statement that the paper never qualifies. dc1 is a genuine conflict with prior work rather than a limitation, and is typed as DSC/comparison with verdict=conflict, correctly. The pH reading that would embarrass the mechanism (c10: GS ends BELOW SBF) is kept on the evidence node rather than spun into an extra audit, which is the right call.
